notes: [abstract only] Sequential Monte Carlo with Bayesian experiment design for Hamiltonian parameters, with numerical Cramer-Rao checks. Adaptive-design alternative to Ch4's fixed k ladder (Ch5 probe-portfolio direction).

title: A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Edward Farhi; Jeffrey Goldstone; Sam Gutmann
notes: [abstract only] Original QAOA; p=1 MaxCut guarantee on 3-regular graphs. Defines the decision family used in Ch4.

title: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for MaxCut: A Fermionic View
authors: Zhihui Wang; Stuart Hadfield; Zhang Jiang; Eleanor G. Rieffel
notes: [abstract only] Closed-form p=1 MaxCut expectation on general graphs. Enables analytic gamma(e) and its gradient for Ch4's decision functional (cross-check for exact simulation; a local-phase-error extension is a possible derivation).

title: Characterizing local noise in QAOA circuits
authors: Jeffrey Marshall; Filip Wudarski; Stuart Hadfield; Tad Hogg
notes: [abstract only] Approximate closed form of QAOA fidelity and cost versus local noise rate, size and depth. Stochastic-noise comparator; does not address coherent native-gate errors or decisions.

title: Effects of Quantum Noise on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Cheng Xue; Zhao-Yun Chen; Yu-Chun Wu; Guo-Ping Guo
notes: [abstract only] Common noise channels flatten the QAOA landscape exponentially but keep optimal parameters nearly fixed. Supports Ch4's depolarization-invariance intuition; coherent errors are the case where this fails.

title: Quantum Approximate Optimization of Non-Planar Graph Problems on a Planar Superconducting Processor
authors: Matthew P. Harrigan; Kevin J. Sung; Matthew Neeley; Kevin J. Satzinger; Frank Arute; Kunal Arya; et al.; Ryan Babbush
notes: [abstract only] Sycamore QAOA up to 23 qubits; hardware-native graphs do not degrade with size, compiled graphs do. Motivates restricting Ch4 instances to hardware-native subgraphs without SWAPs.

title: Limitations of optimization algorithms on noisy quantum devices
authors: Daniel Stilck Franca; Raul Garcia-Patron
notes: [abstract only] Entropic bounds show noisy-device optimization advantage needs much lower noise. Context for why Ch4 restricts claims to decision invariance, not advantage.

title: A Review on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm and its Variants
authors: Kostas Blekos; Dean Brand; Andrea Ceschini; Chiao-Hui Chou; Rui-Hao Li; Komal Pandya; Alessandro Summer
notes: [abstract only] Physics Reports review of QAOA performance, variants and hardware limitations. Survey anchor for the QAOA background section.

title: Provable bounds for noise-free expectation values computed from noisy samples
authors: Samantha V. Barron; Daniel J. Egger; Elijah Pelofske; Andreas Bärtschi; Stephan Eidenbenz; Matthis Lehmkuehler; Stefan Woerner
notes: [abstract only] Risk-based (CVaR) statistic yields provable bounds on noise-free expectation values from noisy IBM samples up to 127 qubits. Closest provable-bound-on-application-output work on IBM; addresses incoherent noise via layer fidelity, not coherent native-gate residuals.

title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
authors: Steven R. Howard; Aaditya Ramdas; Jon McAuliffe; Jasjeet Sekhon
notes: [abstract only] Annals of Statistics; confidence sequences valid at all stopping times without asymptotics. Statistical basis for a sequential, re-certifiable (certificate-lifetime) extension of Ch4.

title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
authors: Ian Waudby-Smith; Aaditya Ramdas
notes: [abstract only] Betting-martingale confidence intervals and sequences for bounded means that beat Hoeffding and empirical Bernstein. Direct candidate to tighten Ch4's finite-sample phase intervals while keeping strict validity.

title: Game-theoretic statistics and safe anytime-valid inference
authors: Aaditya Ramdas; Peter Grünwald; Vladimir Vovk; Glenn Shafer
notes: [abstract only] Review of e-processes and confidence sequences valid under optional stopping. Framework for adaptive or sequential Ch5 certification without losing alpha control.

title: Advances in Quantum Metrology
authors: Vittorio Giovannetti; Seth Lloyd; Lorenzo Maccone
notes: [abstract only] Review of standard-quantum-limit versus Heisenberg scaling and the role of noise. Background for Ch4's k-amplification Fisher analysis (Heisenberg-like scaling until decoherence).

title: Entanglement-free Heisenberg-limited phase estimation
authors: B. L. Higgins; D. W. Berry; S. D. Bartlett; H. M. Wiseman; G. J. Pryde
notes: [abstract only] Repeated application of an unknown phase with a generalized Kitaev scheme reaches Heisenberg scaling without entanglement. Conceptual origin of the repeated-gate k ladder.

title: Characterizing large-scale quantum computers via cycle benchmarking
authors: Alexander Erhard; Joel James Wallman; Lukas Postler; Michael Meth; Roman Stricker; Esteban Adrian Martinez; Philipp Schindler; Thomas Monz; Joseph Emerson; Rainer Blatt
notes: [abstract only] Cycle benchmarking for scalable local and global (crosstalk) error rates under twirling. Twirling is unavailable for fractional gates on IBM, so CB is a comparator whose assumptions Ch4 cannot use directly.

title: Demonstration of qubit operations below a rigorous fault tolerance threshold with gate set tomography
authors: Robin Blume-Kohout; John King Gamble; Erik Nielsen; Kenneth Rudinger; Jonathan Mizrahi; Kevin Fortier; Peter Maunz
notes: [abstract only] GST certifies with over 95% confidence that operations meet a diamond-norm threshold. Precedent for a confidence-qualified threshold certificate; the threshold is generic, not decision-induced.

title: Supplementary information for "Quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor"
authors: Frank Arute; Kunal Arya; Ryan Babbush; Dave Bacon; Joseph C. Bardin; et al.; John M. Martinis
notes: Supplement to the Nature quantum-supremacy paper, documenting device calibration and XEB statistics for fSim gates. [abstract only] Only the version note was reviewed; the calibration details still need full-text confirmation before citation for specific claims.

title: Testing time order and Leggett-Garg inequalities with noninvasive measurements on public quantum computers
authors: Tomasz Rybotycki; Tomasz Białecki; Josep Batle; Bartłomiej Zglinicki; Adam Szereszewski; Wolfgang Belzig; Adam Bednorz
notes: [abstract only] Weak-measurement protocols on five IBM devices using Heron fractional gates show deviations beyond declared error rates. A full-text passage seen in search states fractional RZZ performs significantly worse than fractional RX and that it is ambiguous whether the RZZ strength is accurately reduced; that passage must be read in full before Ch4 cites it as motivation.

title: Evaluating the performance of quantum processing units at large width and depth
authors: J. A. Montanez-Barrera; Kristel Michielsen; David E. Bernal Neira
notes: [abstract only] Linear-ramp QAOA benchmark on 24 QPUs up to 156 qubits and 10,000 layers; full text reports Heron fractional RZZ halves two-qubit depth and improves ibm_fez results. Application-level benchmark that uses native RZZ but reports aggregate approximation ratio, not gate-level decision certificates.

title: Improved Ising Meson Spectroscopy Simulation on a Noisy Digital Quantum Device
authors: Hao-Ti Hung; Isabel Nha Minh Le; Johannes Knolle; Ying-Jer Kao
notes: [abstract only] TFIM Trotter dynamics on ibm_torino with native fractional RZZ/RX versus tensor-network compression; mitigation uses reference circuits keeping RZZ gates. Example of current users relying on fractional RZZ without gate-specific error certificates.

title: A Depth-Independent Linear Chain Ansatz for Large-Scale Quantum Approximate Optimization
authors: Zixu Wang; Jack Mandell; Yangyang Xu; Jian Shi
notes: [abstract only] Linear-chain QAOA with approximation ratio 0.78 on 100-vertex MaxCut; full text compares native RZZ/RX fractional gates with synthesized gates on IBM. Another downstream consumer of native RZZ where decision robustness is not certified.

title: Perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware
authors: Priscilla Awuah; Krystal Guo
notes: [abstract only] Continuous-time quantum-walk state transfer on ibm_kingston without mitigation; full text documents the [0, pi/2] RZZ domain and FoldRzzAngle wrapping. Recent independent confirmation of the angle-domain constraint relevant to G0.

title: Realization and Calibration of Continuously Parameterized Two-Qubit Gates on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Processor
authors: Christopher G. Yale; Ashlyn D. Burch; Matthew N. H. Chow; Brandon P. Ruzic; Daniel S. Lobser; Brian K. McFarland; Melissa C. Revelle; Susan M. Clark
notes: [abstract only] Arbitrary-angle MS gates set by amplitude scaling require calibration of amplifier saturation and light shifts; residual light shifts scale linearly with theta and are cancelled by a dynamic virtual phase. Closest platform analogue: angle-dependent coherent residuals (theta-linear local phase) exactly like Ch4's A(theta) model; IEEE TQE 2025.

title: Noise-Aware Circuit Compilations for a Continuously Parameterized Two-Qubit Gateset
authors: Christopher G. Yale; Rich Rines; Victory Omole; Bharath Thotakura; Ashlyn D. Burch; Matthew N. H. Chow; Megan Ivory; Daniel Lobser; Brian K. McFarland; Melissa C. Revelle; Susan M. Clark; Pranav Gokhale
notes: [abstract only] Noise-aware compilation for arbitrary-angle ZZ gates (minimize total entangling angle, pick best pairs) with analysis of stochastic and coherent error contributions. Shows angle-dependent error is already exploited by compilers; Ch4 adds decision-level certification.

title: Realizing a Continuous Set of Two-Qubit Gates Parameterized by an Idle Time
authors: Colin Scarato; Kilian Hanke; Ants Remm; Stefania Lazăr; Nathan Lacroix; Dante Colao Zanuz; Alexander Flasby; Andreas Wallraff; Christoph Hellings
notes: [abstract only] Controlled arbitrary-phase gates on flux-tunable transmons via idle time in a net-zero pulse; ~0.7% error and 4e-4 leakage across the set, with full text noting angle-dependent error variation. Evidence that continuous two-qubit families have angle-dependent error.

title: Branch-resolved Pauli-block spectroscopy of residual conditional phase in two-qubit gates
authors: Xudan Chai; Yanwu Gu; Huiqi Xue; Kerui Li; Dong E. Liu
notes: Repeated-cycle Pauli-block (IX, IY, ZX, ZY) readout forms control-conditioned branch coherences; nonlocal ZZ shifts the two branch slopes oppositely, local phase shifts them together; echoed variant removes local terms; signed residual recovered; one cloud qubit-coupler pair with pulse-level loop. CRITICAL OVERLAP with Ch4 control-state switching (Section 4) and L2; no finite-sample confidence, no downstream decisions, not native fractional RZZ. Ch4 must cite as prior art for the probe principle. See notes/CHAI2026.md.

title: Structured Hamiltonian Learning for Multiqubit Conditional Phase Gates
authors: Xiu-Hao Deng
notes: Gate/reference Ramsey eigenphase map plus Walsh transform gives the diagonal error generator; branch-independent Boolean-Moebius invariants; Cramer-Rao scaling; finite-shot pass/fail/unresolved decisions under prespecified tolerances with simultaneous confidence; model rejection kept separate from the equivalence decision; seeded simulations only. CRITICAL OVERLAP with C1 and C2 mechanics and OD11 separation; tolerances are gate-equivalence classes, not downstream-decision-induced; no hardware. See notes/DENG2026.md.

title: Sharpening Worst-Case Error Assessment for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: Fidelity and Its Deviation
authors: Kyoungho Cho; Ilkwon Sohn; Yongsoo Hwang; Jeongho Bang
notes: [abstract only] Fidelity deviation across inputs plus average fidelity tightly bounds worst-case error for coherent multi-qubit errors. Shows recent effort to go beyond average fidelity for coherent errors, but targets worst-case FT metrics rather than task decisions.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Processor Performance at Scale
authors: David C. McKay; Ian Hincks; Emily J. Pritchett; Malcolm Carroll; Luke C. G. Govia; Seth T. Merkel
notes: [abstract only] Layer fidelity and EPLG via simultaneous direct RB on Eagle and Heron; linked to runtime and mitigation cost. IBM's platform-level metric; aggregate and twirled, so silent on a specific RZZ angle's coherent residual.

title: When Clifford benchmarks are sufficient; estimating application performance with scalable proxy circuits
authors: Seth Merkel; Timothy Proctor; Samuele Ferracin; Jordan Hines; Samantha Barron; Luke C. G. Govia; David McKay
notes: [abstract only] For errors amenable to Pauli twirling, Clifford proxy circuits approximate fidelity and diamond norm of general circuits; Heron demonstrations. Ch4 operates exactly where the twirling premise fails (fractional gates cannot be twirled), which sharpens Ch4's gap statement.

title: Claim against Measurement: Statistical Artefacts in Quantum Error Mitigation Benchmarks
authors: Dominik Köster; Wolfgang Mauerer
notes: [abstract only] Review of 81 QEM papers finds few inferential statistics; ZNE analysis choices flip conclusions and drift inflates effect sizes more than threefold; proposes minimum reporting standards. Direct support for Ch4's prespecification, drift and inferential-reporting design.

title: Resource-Optimal Screening for Two-Tier Quantum System Characterization
authors: Yi-Ting Chen; Aniket S. Dalvi; Nils Quetschlich
notes: [abstract only] Cheap screening probe triggers full characterization only on significant change; closed-form optimal probe sizes; hardware on three QPUs. Close relative of a Ch5 certificate-lifetime / re-certification trigger design.

title: Principles of quantum functional testing
authors: Nadia Milazzo; Olivier Giraud; Giovanni Gramegna; Daniel Braun
notes: [abstract only] Frames device testing as an accept/reject decision on whether channel parameters lie in producer specifications, using channel iteration, efficient criteria and adaptive design. Quantum precedent for decision-oriented testing with repeated channel use; specs are producer-given, not induced by a downstream task.

title: Classification testing: A new framework for drawing qualitative conclusions from quantitative estimates
authors: Andrew C. Eggers; Zikai Li
notes: [abstract only] Assigns an estimand to researcher-defined qualitative classes with hypothesis-test-like error control and an inconclusive outcome. Generalizes Ch4's harmless/harmful/inconclusive rule; C2's generic logic must cite this and TOST.

title: Precision-Guaranteed Quantum Metrology
authors: Takanori Sugiyama
notes: [abstract only] Rigorous finite-data error upper bound for quantum parameter estimation that keeps Heisenberg scaling; Ramsey example. Direct precedent for finite-sample-valid phase bounds in amplified Ramsey sequences.

title: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
authors: Tim P. Morris; Ian R. White; Michael J. Crowther
notes: [abstract only] Statistics in Medicine 38(11):2074-2102. Defines the ADEMP structure (aims, data-generating mechanisms, estimands, methods, performance measures) and Monte Carlo standard-error reporting. Direct source for Ch4 Section 9 and WP6.

title: Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables
authors: Wassily Hoeffding
notes: [abstract only] JASA 58(301):13-30. Concentration inequality used for the finite-sample phase intervals in src/estimate.py.

title: Bioequivalence trials, intersection-union tests and equivalence confidence sets
authors: Roger L. Berger; Jason C. Hsu
notes: [abstract only] Statistical Science 11(4):283-319. IUT theory unifies TOST, gives more powerful size-alpha tests, and corrects the 1-2alpha confidence-set misconception. Required citation for the size claims of Ch4's two one-sided bounds.

title: The use of confidence or fiducial limits illustrated in the case of the binomial
authors: C. J. Clopper; E. S. Pearson
notes: [abstract only] Biometrika 26(4):404-413. Exact binomial confidence limits; tighter alternative to Hoeffding for per-circuit counts.

title: Interval Estimation for a Binomial Proportion
authors: Lawrence D. Brown; T. Tony Cai; Anirban DasGupta
notes: [abstract only] Statistical Science 16(2):101-133. Coverage oscillation of Wald and exact binomial intervals. Justifies preferring exact or concentration bounds over Wald in the primary analysis.

title: Decision Analysis and Bioequivalence Trials
authors: Dennis V. Lindley
notes: [abstract only] Statistical Science 13(2):136-141. Argues bioequivalence is a decision problem better handled by expected loss than by tests or intervals. Principled counterpoint to Ch4's frequentist rule; motivates a Bayesian decision-theoretic secondary analysis or discussion.

title: Quantum computing with Qiskit
authors: Ali Javadi-Abhari; Matthew Treinish; Kevin Krsulich; Christopher J. Wood; Jake Lishman; Julien Gacon; Simon Martiel; Paul D. Nation; Lev S. Bishop; Andrew W. Cross; Blake R. Johnson; Jay M. Gambetta
notes: [abstract only] Authoritative citation for the Qiskit SDK, its transpiler architecture and retargetability to new gates. Software citation for WP3/WP7 and for transpiler-behaviour claims (FoldRzzAngle must additionally cite version-pinned runtime docs).

title: Measuring the Capabilities of Quantum Computers
authors: Timothy Proctor; Kenneth Rudinger; Kevin Young; Erik Nielsen; Robin Blume-Kohout
notes: [abstract only] Mirror-circuit capability regions on twelve processors, dividing width-depth space into success, indeterminate and fail; standard error metrics poorly predict program success. Close conceptual analogue of a three-outcome application-level verdict (Nature Physics 2022).

title: Stability of noisy quantum computing devices
authors: Samudra Dasgupta; Travis S. Humble
notes: [abstract only] Hellinger-distance stability of NISQ performance metrics over time; fluctuations undermine reproducibility. Background for G6 replication and for certificate lifetime.

title: Impact of unreliable devices on stability of quantum computations
authors: Samudra Dasgupta; Travis S. Humble
notes: [abstract only] Device-characterization similarity metrics yield bounds on the stability of an algorithm's output (Bernstein-Vazirani). Precedent for bounding algorithm-level output stability from device data, in a non-certification, non-decision setting.
